why: Display (22) and touch (23) are proven, so this is the next gate: every app-level screen sits on LVGL, and it settles draw-buffer size and placement (PSRAM vs internal DMA) against the measured 24 ms full-frame fill.
Gates running on battery in the case: BAT_Control (IO7) is a power-hold latch, so without firmware driving it the board turns off when PWR is released. Small, and the board is on the bench.
Hardware track, can run alongside firmware: the back cup fits (15) but nothing holds the glass until a front closes onto it. Starts with measuring what fouled v1, not remodelling.
Cheap win once 24 is in: both chips already answer on I2C (0x51 RTC, 0x6b IMU). The RTC keeps time across power cycles; the IMU can drive raise-to-wake later.
